reason: Live check of a dashboard change copied two edited files into the shared main checkout, and cleanup failed to restore them for about two minutes. No skill covers live verification of a worktree change against seeded local fixtures, so the rule and the seeding recipe belong in one place.

The user-lens verification of the sign-in loop hit three traps not in the skill: the default preview config bypasses auth, a cold compile looked like a blank page, and a stale cookie kept the loop running. Each cost a re-run, so the recipe belongs with the existing live-verify steps.

Verifying a server-rendered, zone-dependent value (the dashboard "today" tile and header zone label) was faster and deterministic with curl and a Cookie header on the worktree server, with the server pinned to TZ=UTC to mirror Vercel. The browser pane also came back empty while hidden, and the cookie jar was shared with the main session and browser subagents.

This episode could not get :3100 or :3200 (peer sessions held them) and had to ship as not live-verified. The skill should say what to do in that case, so the next session does not verify on the production-pointed port.

This session re-learned four live-check facts: fixtures go stale at local midnight, the in-app browser is pinned to HKT so other organiser zones need a Playwright context, the TZ=UTC launch config must be reverted, and before/after proof works best as one grid. Add them beside the existing zone bullets.

Viewport and colour-scheme emulation carried past the check and survived reloads; the tool tells you to reset it. The 375 px overflow read is the cheap check that caught nothing wrong this time but is the one to repeat.

While a browser reviewer walked the shared :3100 dev server, the orchestrator held its edit to lib/auth.ts because hot reload would change the screens under the reviewer mid-walk. That rule is missing from the live-verify skill and will recur whenever a reviewer and an edit share the server.
Two reviewers' walks left audit rows after cleanup; the skill's zero-leftover check would read that as a failed cleanup without this note.

The episode hit a peer-held :3100 lock mid-live-check. The skill covered blocked ports but not the lock-file etiquette (message the holder, background-wait, respect the shared cookie jar), which is what the session actually did.
A closing cleanup ran an unconditional rm -f on the shared :3100 lock, which could have deleted a peer's claim. The skill already says peers hold this lock, so the release rule belongs here.

DB-02 user-lens reviewer was briefed "do NOT start or stop any server", hit a dead :3100, and handed back PARTIAL. The coordinator had to restart the server and resume the reviewer. A background watcher also timed out and exited 0 ("STILL DOWN after 240s [exited with code 0]"), which read as success.

Reviewer hand-back warned that :3100 in review mode makes signed-out staff pages open, so an auth walk run signed-out gives a false pass. The skill covers the preview config but has no probe to detect the mode before a walk.

Episode verified the /events listing fix by fetching the page with curl and comparing HTML card links and titles to the local DB (21 of 21 upcoming present, 0 of 227 past present). That recipe is reusable for any public list page and was not in the skill. It also left a dev server running without saying so in the hand-back.

A production-mode backtest surfaced three gaps not in this skill: branches gated on NODE_ENV=production never fire on a dev server; /login is magic-link only so the auth walk needs a minted session cookie; and a cron/dispatch tick writes rows for every local event, not just fixtures, so cleanup must be scoped by error signature.

A live zone walk embedded a test session cookie in a run_code script; the tool echoed the script into chat. The skill's rule covers cookies in scratch files but not this echo. Cookie reuse across ports is also a real trap in the same walk.

A user-lens reviewer reported "no response" on Send reminders now. The button had opened a confirm dialog that its scripted clicks never answered. The live-verify skill should say to handle dialogs before reporting a dead button.

The viewport emulation was cleared mid-check when the pane changed width. The tool output said so, but a click by coordinates after that would land on the wrong layout. Make the re-screenshot step explicit in the live-verify recipe.

Within one session the pane showed a stale render after parts.tsx changed on disk; measurements taken before a reload were wrong until the tab was reloaded. Live-verify skill has no reload-after-edit rule.

Dark-mode live check failed twice through the easy routes (colour-scheme emulation and a data-theme attribute); the key-plus-reload route worked. The skill covers the reset but not how to enter dark mode, so the next session repeats the dead ends.

The UX-02 backtest could not click Sign out because /account/complete never hydrated in the pane. The agent proved the server side with curl instead. That fallback, and the rule to label the click step unverified, are not in the skill yet.
A user-lens walk lost most of its call budget to coordinate clicks after Playwright MCP refused to start. Clicking by ref is the working path on the built-in browser.

The description is the trigger. This skill is the one that handles browser-lock and form-fill problems in Eventar live walks, but its description does not name them, so it would not route on those words.

The lock-holder check was missing. A walk saw several playwright-mcp processes from other sessions and correctly left them alone. That check should be a step in the skill, so the next session does not kill a peer's browser or retry in a loop.

A create form's scripted fill and keyboard venue pick both failed in a walk, and the lost step was not worth the calls. The skill should say how to fill a custom form and how to report a failed fill, so the next walk does not repeat the same loop.

The organiser walk lost a step to a guessed table name and lost roughly 30 calls and a timezone correctness check to an async venue picker. Both are live-verification traps this skill covers only in part (it has the click-by-ref rule but not the async-list or table-lookup cases).
A persona-role join guessed the staff key column and errored; the column must be read before the join, the same rule the table-name bullet already states.
A registration walk on a past-dated fixture hit a closed registration; the fix (shift the start to the future) is a repeatable step the skill does not yet name.
The walk attributed its results to a persona by reading the last Mailpit message, which is not evidence of the live session; the rule is that identity is verified, not inferred.

This episode signed the browser in through the Mailpit magic link instead of cookie injection, and it worked first time. The live-verify skill mentions Mailpit only as a source of the last-requested address, so a future walk would not know the sign-in path. The recipe includes the To-address check that stops a peer's link being used.

The walk asked for a screenshot per step, the built-in browser could not write files, and the summary had to declare the per-step screenshot requirement unmet on disk. The skill named inline screenshots but did not say how to report a shortfall, so a future walk could claim screenshots it does not have.
